opening.text: Saturday is Women’s Day. In the town, men bring flowers. On my round, the florist has no flowers until spring.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: So you bring sweets.

opening.speaker: sorin
opening.text: To the whole night ward. Ana says that nurses accept sweets on behalf of everyone.

completion.speaker: ana
completion.text: The nurses thank you, Sorin. The doctor tried to accept a papanaș on behalf of the nurses. We stopped him.

completion.speaker: sorin
completion.text: Next year I will bring more, and a lock for the box.

opening.speaker: victor
opening.text: My professor wants proof that I can keep something alive all night. Two eggs and a linden tea should keep me alive, at least.

completion.speaker: victor
completion.text: It worked. I was alive at sunrise, and the professor is very impressed. He expected a frog.

opening.speaker: eszter
opening.text: My best glaze yet is in the kiln. If I open it early, it cracks.

opening.speaker: eszter
opening.text: So bring me something to eat standing up. My hands need a job.

completion.speaker: eszter
completion.text: It opened, and nothing cracked. Look at that blue.

completion.speaker: sorin
completion.text: She was patient for almost the whole hour. I counted.

opening.speaker: costel
opening.text: Sunday is the day of the Forty Martyrs. The custom asks for mucenici, and forty small glasses of wine for each man. I tried it once. My pocket clock counted the glasses and stopped at nine. Mucenici and a socată, please.

completion.speaker: costel
completion.text: The mucenici were perfect, and my clock still works. This year, I counted socată.

opening.speaker: sorin
opening.text: On every street of my round, people ask what we will cook here. I keep saying "soon".

opening.speaker: sorin
opening.text: Give me a quick lunch at the counter, and I will have a better answer.

completion.speaker: sorin
completion.text: Now I can tell them. Bread that is still warm, potatoes from the new crate, and socată that is cold.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: Tell them to come and taste it. That works better than a description.

opening.speaker: adrian
opening.text: The old cathedral on the hill has a staircase behind the altar. It goes down further than the hill is tall.

opening.speaker: sorin
opening.text: I pass it on my round. At night, it groans. I always thought that it was the wind.

opening.speaker: adrian
opening.text: There is no wind under a cathedral. We will go down and look, and we need food for several days.

completion.speaker: adrian
completion.text: The pack is full. If we are not back in a week, do not send anyone. Send more pogăcele.

opening.speaker: costel
opening.text: The church clock stopped at half past three. Until I mend it, it is always teatime. Two papanași, please, and a plum for the pendulum. A clock likes things in pairs.

completion.speaker: costel
completion.text: The clock runs again. I set it five minutes fast, so nobody is ever late for dessert.

opening.speaker: dochia
opening.text: Spring is close, and I am down to three sheepskins. Bulz, smoked cheese, langoș, and linden tea, and I will give up another without a fight.

completion.speaker: dochia
completion.text: Done. If it snows tomorrow, I am blaming you.

opening.speaker: dochia
opening.text: The first lambs came in the night, two of them in the snow. I will sleep in the fold until the rest arrive. Telemea, bread, and hot tea, please. It is a long watch.

completion.speaker: dochia
completion.text: Seven lambs, all on their feet. The smallest one sleeps inside my coat. That makes ten sheepskins, and the weather is furious.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: The long table is ready. What if people sit at the far ends and nobody talks?

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: Then put the food in the middle. People always lean in for food.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: A fruit bowl, then, and a few plates beside it. Something that everyone has to pass.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: They passed it, and they talked. You were right, Ilie.

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: My grandmother was right. I only remembered.

opening.speaker: ileana
opening.text: I have three wedding dresses to finish before Thursday. Fruit tea, cherry compote, and whatever the butcher and the market sent, please, before I sew a sleeve shut by mistake.

completion.speaker: ileana
completion.text: All three dresses are done. Joimărița can inspect my house whenever she likes.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: In this village, a candle in the window means that the door is open to anyone.

opening.speaker: sorin
opening.text: On my round, only three houses still do it. The others stopped years ago.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Then we will be the fourth. Let us light ours and have supper beside it.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: Two neighbours waved, and one of them came in.

completion.speaker: sorin
completion.text: And an owl stared all evening. Nobody invited it. It came anyway.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: On Saturday, we hold Mamaia’s three-month memorial. Mama cannot come from the city, so the memorial is mine.

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: In Lent, the church remembers the dead on Saturdays anyway. She will have company.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Colivă for the church, colaci for the people at the gate, and pickled cabbage as she made it. She always fed the priest, and it is Lent.

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: The priest read her name first. Then he read it again, more slowly. He wanted a second colac.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: Half the village came to the gate. Each person told me a different reason why she fed them.

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: All the reasons were true. That was your grandmother.

opening.speaker: monica
opening.text: We are back from the first floors under the cathedral. Dust, bones, and a very large cook with a cleaver.

opening.speaker: monica
opening.text: He shouted about fresh meat and chased Adrian up two flights of stairs.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: A cook? Did he say where he trained?

opening.speaker: monica
opening.text: We did not stop to ask. This time, we bring him something better than Adrian.

completion.speaker: monica
completion.text: We will leave the sausages on the stairs for him. A cook that busy never gets a hot meal.

opening.speaker: vlad
opening.text: Book my table for eight in the evening. I dine only after sunset, an old family habit. Smoked bacon and two carafes of red wine, if you please. No garlic, naturally.

completion.speaker: vlad
completion.text: Excellent. The wine is exactly the right shade of red. I am very particular about red.

opening.speaker: elisabeta
opening.text: A table at eight in the evening, please, and not on the same evening as my neighbour. He has moved the fence between our lands again. Roast pork, chicken broth, and red wine. Red helps me read estate papers.

completion.speaker: elisabeta
completion.text: The papers are in order. My neighbour’s boundary has moved a little toward my land. How odd.

opening.speaker: vlad
opening.text: A guest from abroad comes to my castle soon, on a matter of property. Book my table for eight in the evening, on a night when the countess is not here. I must give him roast pork, tochitură, and plenty of red wine. First impressions matter.

completion.speaker: vlad
completion.text: Splendid. My guest will feel very welcome. Nobody ever wants to leave my castle. Nobody ever does.

opening.speaker: eszter
opening.text: Every place at the table has a bowl and a cup. Now the small sweet plate needs its place.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Does it have to be exact?

opening.speaker: eszter
opening.text: It has to look as if it was always there. Bring sweets, and I will move it until it does.

completion.speaker: eszter
completion.text: There. Bowl, cup, plate, and nothing crowds anything.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: You moved it eleven times.

completion.speaker: eszter
completion.text: Twelve. The last time was the right one.

opening.speaker: eszter
opening.text: I fired a second set of bowls with a green glaze. Ilie says that blue is traditional.

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: My grandmother had blue bowls.

opening.speaker: eszter
opening.text: Your grandmother never saw this green. Fill them, and let the food decide.

completion.speaker: eszter
completion.text: The food likes both. Keep the green bowls with the blue ones.

completion.speaker: eszter
completion.text: Tap the bowls on the upper shelf to change them whenever you like.

opening.speaker: cezar
opening.text: My round ends at dawn. Tochitură and roasted vegetables would make a fine breakfast. Or supper. Whichever this is. A second tochitură, please, for the walk home.

completion.speaker: cezar
completion.text: Very good. I will eat it on the way home. My feet know the way.

opening.speaker: janos
opening.text: The cook ate all the sausages and fell asleep on his cleaver. We walked straight past him.

opening.speaker: janos
opening.text: Deeper under the cathedral, a king of bones sits on a stone throne. He still wears his crown, and he still asks for taxes.

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: In coins?

opening.speaker: janos
opening.text: In bread, it seems. I want to read the marks on his throne, and that is a long reading.

completion.speaker: janos
completion.text: Sit a while, and listen, I will tell him. Then I will read him his own family history. Nobody stays awake for that.

opening.speaker: sorin
opening.text: Everyone in the valley is sending letters this week, and every one of them lives up a hill.

opening.speaker: sorin
opening.text: One letter has no name. Only an address: "the house that is not there".

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Eat first. Then decide what to do with it.

completion.speaker: sorin
completion.text: Every letter is delivered. I left the strange one at the crossroads, and by morning it was gone.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: Was there a reply?

completion.speaker: sorin
completion.text: A dry leaf, folded like a letter. I am not delivering that.

opening.speaker: ana
opening.text: The night patients cannot sleep. A linden tea for them, please, and a proper supper for the porter.

completion.speaker: ana
completion.text: The whole ward is asleep. Even the porter. Especially the porter.

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: Tuesday is the Annunciation. In Lent it is the first day with fish, and my grandmother never missed it.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: The fish trap gave us two trout this morning.

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: Then two trout over the coals, and white beans beside them. The cuckoo sings for the first time on this day, too.

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: The cuckoo sang while I ate. I counted eleven calls.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: What does eleven mean?

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: That I ate slowly.

opening.speaker: dorian
opening.text: A gallery is showing my portrait on Friday. I have invited a few friends to admire it. A cheese board, a cozonac, and red wine for the guests, please.

completion.speaker: dorian
completion.text: Everyone admired the portrait. One guest said that its eyes followed her around the room. I hope that she found them attentive.

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: We have a courtyard now. My family never ate outside. My grandmother said that the air makes bread stale.

opening.speaker: sorin
opening.text: Your grandmother never had a langoș in the sun.

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: Bring one, then, and a socată. I will find the place where it stays soft.

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: By the kitchen door, in the shade. Still warm, and still soft.

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: I will add a line to her notebook. In small letters.

opening.speaker: sorin
opening.text: Before a guest walks the courtyard, I walk it with a full tray. Gate, door, tables.

opening.speaker: eszter
opening.text: And if you trip?

opening.speaker: sorin
opening.text: Then you will hear it. Put roasted vegetables on the tray, and nettles from the wall. If the route is bad, I want to drop something cheap.

completion.speaker: sorin
completion.text: Not one loose stone. The tray reached every chair.

completion.speaker: eszter
completion.text: And then you ate the test.

completion.speaker: sorin
completion.text: A test needs a result.

opening.speaker: bran
opening.text: The last bus leaves the square at midnight. Nobody gets on after the bridge, but I stop anyway. A langoș and a bulz for the road, please, and a piece of lamb. The lamb is for the horse. Do not ask.

completion.speaker: bran
completion.text: Thank you. The road through the woods is long, and I like company. Even the quiet kind.

opening.speaker: adrian
opening.text: The bone king fell asleep at chapter two, as Janos promised. Under his throne, the cathedral has catacombs.

opening.speaker: adrian
opening.text: A small goblin lives down there. He begs for mercy whenever he sees us, and he keeps promising us a gift.

opening.speaker: sorin
opening.text: What is the gift?

opening.speaker: adrian
opening.text: So far, a rock. We will keep watch down there for several nights, so we need proper suppers.

completion.speaker: adrian
completion.text: Most of the bread is for us. One bread basket is for the goblin. Perhaps he will give us a better rock.

opening.speaker: dochia
opening.text: The snow is leaving the high pasture, and the flock wants to climb before I do. Pack enough for the shepherds, the dogs, and me. The ram carries nothing. He says that it is beneath him.

completion.speaker: dochia
completion.text: We reached the high pasture. At the top I took off my last sheepskin, and the wind put it back on me. Next March, then.

opening.speaker: dorian
opening.text: A gentleman from the castle has invited me to a candlelit supper. Cozonac, a cheese board, and red wine, please. His evenings tend to last until dawn.

completion.speaker: dorian
completion.text: A charming evening. My host had no mirrors, so I checked my cravat in a spoon. One must make an effort for good company.

opening.speaker: eszter
opening.text: The new kiln is finished. Potters celebrate by watching it heat up.

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: For how long?

opening.speaker: eszter
opening.text: Three hours. Bring food for two. You are invited.

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: We watched it for three hours.

completion.speaker: eszter
completion.text: And?

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: The best party of the year. Do not tell anyone that I said that.

opening.speaker: victor
opening.text: I finished my thesis at three in the morning, during a thunderstorm. Bring the best of the menu, please. We are celebrating.

completion.speaker: victor
completion.text: My thesis passed. The examiners said it has a life of its own. I am choosing to take that as praise.

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: I built new shelves in the cellar, to my grandfather’s plan. Something keeps moving the jars to the left.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Mice?

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: Mice do not line them up. I will eat a fasting supper down there and watch.

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: The jars stayed still while I ate. When I went upstairs, they moved again.

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: We have agreed to share. My jars on the right, and whoever it is on the left.

opening.speaker: monica
opening.text: The goblin kept his promise. The rock is a map now. He scratched it himself.

opening.speaker: monica
opening.text: It shows caves under the cathedral catacombs, and a stream that runs all the way up to your village well.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: So that is why the well water tastes of matches on some mornings.

opening.speaker: monica
opening.text: We will follow the stream. It is a long path, so we need a large pack.

completion.speaker: monica
completion.text: Packed. Until we come back, do not drink from the well. Drink cherry compote. It is safer, and it is cherry compote.

opening.speaker: elisabeta
opening.text: I am taking the evening off for a long bath at my manor. Afterwards, a table at eight, please: roast lamb, tochitură, and a carafe of red wine. Do not ask what is in the bath. Rose petals. Only rose petals.

completion.speaker: elisabeta
completion.text: Wonderful. My maids say that I look younger every year. I tell them that it is the tochitură.

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: My great-aunt’s zacuscă is in the family notebook. She wrote "a good amount of peppers".

opening.speaker: eszter
opening.text: How many peppers is a good amount?

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: Nobody knows. Bring a jar, and lentils beside it, and we will decide for the family.

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: This is a good amount. I will write it in numbers, beside her words, for the tasting.

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: The next cook will not have to guess. She would hate that. She loved a mystery.

opening.speaker: cezar
opening.text: Somebody keeps lighting candles in the castle on the hill. It is not my district, but I like to watch with a warm plate. Veal from the new butcher’s block, a bean soup, and a tochitură, please.

completion.speaker: cezar
completion.text: The candles went out at midnight. I stayed awake for all of it. Well, for most of it.

opening.speaker: dorian
opening.text: The painter wants spring light for a new portrait. Tell me honestly, Mara: does my old portrait look tired lately? Cozonac, a cheese board, and red wine, please, while you decide.

completion.speaker: dorian
completion.text: The painter says that I look exactly as I did forty years ago. He meant it kindly, so I paid him twice. The old portrait sighed. I heard it from the stairs.

opening.speaker: sanziana
opening.text: On Sunday I sell willow catkins at the church gate. Fish is allowed on Palm Sunday, so I buy it for my sisters. My sisters share very well. Nobody has ever seen them eat.

completion.speaker: sanziana
completion.text: The catkins are blessed, and the trout are gone. A branch of catkins is for your window. It keeps the storms away, or at least it says so.

opening.speaker: eszter
opening.text: I glazed the tasting plates to match the long table. One plum dumpling and a little cozonac will show me if they are large enough.

opening.speaker: sorin
opening.text: And if they are too small?

opening.speaker: eszter
opening.text: Then the dumpling is too large. My plates are correct.

completion.speaker: eszter
completion.text: Room for the dumpling and its label. I was right.

completion.speaker: sorin
completion.text: The plates were right. I will clear the test.

quests.title: Holy Week on the night bus

opening.speaker: bran
opening.text: In Holy Week, pilgrims fill the night bus. They sing all the way to the monastery, and they ate all my langoș. Two more, please, and a bean soup in a bread bowl.

completion.speaker: bran
completion.text: The pilgrims blessed the bus, the horse, and my scarf. The scarf did not need it, but thank you.

opening.speaker: janos
opening.text: Your well is clean again. Monica moved a family of very damp lizards out of the stream.

opening.speaker: janos
opening.text: Below the caves, under the cathedral, I found a letter from the archbishop who left this village forty years ago.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: With the money for the church roof. My grandmother never forgave him.

opening.speaker: janos
opening.text: She was right. In the letter, he writes to someone further down, and he calls them “my lord”.

completion.speaker: janos
completion.text: We will read the rest in the library down there. Its librarian screams when anyone turns a page, but a chimney cake keeps him quiet.

opening.speaker: ileana
opening.text: Thursday is close, and my brother has not touched his spindle. I am taking him zacuscă toast and a langoș, so that he has no excuse.

completion.speaker: ileana
completion.text: He spun all night. Nothing was burned, and nobody had a visitor. A good week.

opening.speaker: costel
opening.text: I have finished a dancing doll for the village fair. She dances very well, but she stares a little. Cozonac, papanași, and a plum brandy to celebrate?

completion.speaker: costel
completion.text: She danced through the whole fair. Only one child cried, and that was because the cozonac ran out.

opening.speaker: bran
opening.text: On my day off, I ride through the woods. The horse wants apples. I want zacuscă toast, diced veal, and langoș.

completion.speaker: bran
completion.text: A fine ride. People ran off the road when they saw us, but I think that was the horse. It is very tall.

opening.speaker: catalina
opening.text: A stranger with a long beard and a book is asking about the weather. I do not like it. Green beans and plum dumplings, so that I can keep watch from the tower.

completion.speaker: catalina
completion.text: He rode off on a very dark cloud. The weather is fine now. Thank you for the plum dumplings.

opening.speaker: dorian
opening.text: It is my birthday. I will not say which one. Cozonac, a cheese board, and a glass of red wine, please, and no candles. There are never enough.

completion.speaker: dorian
completion.text: Thank you. The portrait in my attic sends its regards. It had a much harder day than I did.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Tonight the baskets go to the church for the blessing at midnight: pască, red eggs, cozonac, and drob, under an embroidered towel.

opening.speaker: eszter
opening.text: I wove the towels. Sorin carries the candle.

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: And I guard the baskets until midnight. I will not taste. Lent is not over.

completion.speaker: sorin
completion.text: The priest blessed every basket, and the candle stayed lit the whole way home.

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: I did not taste. I smelled. Smelling is not in the rules.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: Tomorrow, Ilie. Tomorrow you eat first.

opening.speaker: catalina
opening.text: From Holy Thursday until Easter night, the bells rest, and the wooden toaca calls the village. I have nothing to ring, and my hands do not know what to do. Bean dip, green beans, and plum dumplings, please.

completion.speaker: catalina
completion.text: I tapped the toaca very politely. Then I sat on my hands until Easter. At midnight I rang so loud that the next valley woke up.

opening.speaker: sorin
opening.text: The April rain turned the forest road to mud. It came up to my pedals, and then to my knees.

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: Take the town road.

opening.speaker: sorin
opening.text: The town road has the same mud and more dogs. Something warm, please, before I go back out.

completion.speaker: sorin
completion.text: Delivered. The bicycle is still in the forest. It decided to stay.

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: I will lend you the cart.

completion.speaker: sorin
completion.text: The cart has more sense. It refused.

opening.speaker: adrian
opening.text: Below the library, the stone under the cathedral turns red and warm. Ilie, you could bake bread on those walls.

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: Is the heat even?

opening.speaker: adrian
opening.text: Hotter at the back, like your stove. The archbishop is down there. He preaches to an empty hall, and we need one more stay to learn who listens.

completion.speaker: adrian
completion.text: That covers the stay. If you hear a bell ring under the hill, it is only the archbishop. Probably.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Christ is risen, Ilie. The fast is over, and the staff eat together today.

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: Truly he is risen. Seven weeks of beans, Mara. Last night I dreamed of lamb, and the lamb was very polite about it.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Then lamb, drob, red eggs, and cozonac. You eat first.

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: I ate first, and then second. Then I knocked eggs with Sorin and lost every time.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: He holds his egg with the point down. It is a trick.

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: It is a sin. A small one. It is Easter.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: I have a bad dream about the supper. The fish reaches the table while the cheese waits.

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: In my family, the cheese always went first.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Tonight, both go together. Let us practise one service.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: Together, at last. Now I can watch the guests, not the kitchen door.

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: The cheese still went first. By one step.

opening.speaker: sorin
opening.text: I know every door on my round. On the supper night, I want to meet each one of them at the gate.

opening.speaker: sorin
opening.text: A meal ready for the first guests who arrive tired from the hill.

completion.speaker: sorin
completion.text: For years, people on my round asked me in for a meal. Tonight, I give each of them one back.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: And then you sit down too.

completion.speaker: sorin
completion.text: Then I sit down too.

opening.speaker: eszter
opening.text: On Easter Monday, the young men visit with cologne and sprinkle the girls, so that they do not wilt. Then the girls give them red eggs.

opening.speaker: sorin
opening.text: I have a bottle of cologne. A large one.

opening.speaker: eszter
opening.text: A drop is enough, Sorin. One drop.

completion.speaker: eszter
completion.text: I smell like a whole flower market. The cats will not come near me.

completion.speaker: sorin
completion.text: Nobody will wilt this year.

completion.speaker: eszter
completion.text: Nobody in the valley. Here is your egg.

opening.speaker: ana
opening.text: Tuesday is Saint George’s Eve, when the witches and the strigoi walk. It is my turn to hang garlic on every door of the ward. That is a lot of doors. Langoș, pogăcele, and a linden tea, please, before I start.

completion.speaker: ana
completion.text: Every door has its garlic. The ward smells terrible, and nothing knocked all night. Perfect.

opening.speaker: ileana
opening.text: I am embroidering the towels for the supper gate. Bring stuffed peppers and a fried trout, and I will finish the last corner.

completion.speaker: ileana
completion.text: The towels are done. Each corner has a little red rooster. They keep watch better than Cezar.

opening.speaker: monica
opening.text: Nobody listens to the archbishop. He preaches to a door, a great red door at the very bottom, sixteen floors under the cathedral.

opening.speaker: monica
opening.text: Behind it, something snores. The stones shake with each breath.

opening.speaker: sorin
opening.text: So that is the groaning that I hear on my round.

opening.speaker: monica
opening.text: That is the groaning. We go back carefully, and this time we do not knock.

completion.speaker: monica
completion.text: The meatballs are for the archbishop. A man who preaches that long must be hungry, and a full man preaches less.

opening.speaker: cezar
opening.text: Last night I woke up in your courtyard with an empty plate. I do not remember eating. Tochitură, mici, and cabbage rolls, please, so that I remember this time.

completion.speaker: cezar
completion.text: I remember every bite. Thank you. If you see me in the courtyard tonight, please wave.

opening.speaker: ileana
opening.text: I embroidered a blue cloth for the serving table. Let us test it with zacuscă and a zacuscă toast. The stains will tell us if it is ready.

completion.speaker: ileana
completion.text: Not a single stain. The blue cloth is yours too. Tap the serving table in the courtyard to change the cloth whenever you like.

opening.speaker: janos
opening.text: The archbishop ate the meatballs and fell asleep in the middle of a sermon. I borrowed his loose pages.

opening.speaker: janos
opening.text: They name what sleeps behind the red door under the cathedral. I will not say that name in a kitchen.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Will it wake up?

opening.speaker: janos
opening.text: Not this year, if nobody knocks. We need a few quiet days to read the rest.

completion.speaker: janos
completion.text: We will read the last pages down there. When we come back, we will tell you everything over a proper meal.

completion.speaker: janos
completion.text: Until then, if a stranger asks for the way to a red door, send him to the bistro for cozonac.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Today is the Easter of the Blajini. Mamaia Paraschiva always took food to the graves and floated the eggshells down the river.

opening.speaker: bela
opening.text: Good evening. I opened the churchyard gate early for you. Forgive me, but what is a Blajin?

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Gentle little people at the edge of the world. They live so far away that they never hear when Easter comes. The shells tell them.

completion.speaker: bela
completion.text: The shells went down the river in a neat line. The graves were very pleased with the colivă.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: You can tell?

completion.speaker: bela
completion.text: After thirty years, you can always tell.

opening.speaker: catalina
opening.text: For the supper, I will ring the bell to call everyone in. That is a lot of rope to pull. Saramură with mămăligă, bean stew, and plum dumplings, please.

completion.speaker: catalina
completion.text: I will ring it loud enough for the whole valley. The next valley too, if they bring a dish.

opening.speaker: sanziana
opening.text: Wildflowers are lovely, but lilacs smell like the evening. Bring plum dumplings, roasted vegetables, and fruit tea, and I will bring an armful.

completion.speaker: sanziana
completion.text: The lilacs are ready. When the supper starts, tap the jug on the dresser in the front room to change the flowers whenever you like.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Every quest is delivered, and every table is set. Only the supper itself is left to cook: one plate for each guest, to each one’s taste.

opening.speaker: sorin
opening.text: I asked on my round. Vlad and Elisabeta sent their regrets. They do not eat supper, they said. Not this kind.

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: Then we are eleven, and the courtyard has ten seats.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: I will stand. A host never sits until the pot is empty. Tonight the bistro cooks, and nobody pays a coin.

opening.speaker: ionatan
opening.text: I have come from abroad to close a real-estate deal with a local noble at the nearby castle. I reach it tomorrow night. Before I continue, I would like a proper dinner.

completion.speaker: ionatan
completion.text: An excellent dinner. Here is the payment, with my thanks. My papers are in order, and I must leave for the castle now. My journey takes me on from there, so I will not return. Farewell.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: May has barely started, and the kitchen is already an oven. The stove heats the room more than the pots.

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: My grandmother cooked in the summer kitchen from May to September. Only the bread stayed indoors.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Then today we eat something cold and look at the shed. Zacuscă on toast, a cheese pie, and a cold socată.

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: Cold food on a hot day. You are learning.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: I ate it in the door of the shed. There is a stove in there, under a heap of sacks.

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: Mamaia’s old stove. It sulks too, I expect.

opening.speaker: sorin
opening.text: On my round, I pass the old orchard behind the bistro. Last night every tree creaked, and there was no wind.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Old trees creak.

opening.speaker: sorin
opening.text: They creaked in turns, Mara, like a choir. Something to eat, please, before I take the long way round.

completion.speaker: sorin
completion.text: I asked at the shop. The orchard belongs to the cathedral. Nobody buys it, because of the creaking.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: Does anybody know the price?

completion.speaker: sorin
completion.text: The shopkeeper knows the price of everything in the village. She did not know this one.

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: My family notebook has a page about clay ovens. My great-grandmother baked in one every summer.

opening.speaker: eszter
opening.text: What does the page say?

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: Mostly that her oven was better than her sister’s. Feed me, and I will look for the useful lines.

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: Here: “Straw, clay, and patience. The oven knows if you hurry.” That is the whole recipe.

completion.speaker: eszter
completion.text: That is my whole trade.

opening.speaker: ileana
opening.text: Every woman in the village wants a new embroidered blouse for the day of the blouse, on 24 June. I have eleven orders and two hands. Zacuscă toast, fruit tea, and roasted vegetables, please. I sew faster when I am fed.

completion.speaker: ileana
completion.text: Eleven blouses are cut. My brother offered to help, so I gave him the buttons. He is still counting them.

opening.speaker: cezar
opening.text: The nights get shorter in May, and my round stays the same length. So I walk faster, or I rest my eyes less. A bean soup, mici, and a langoș, please.

completion.speaker: cezar
completion.text: I walked faster. I finished my round twenty minutes early, so I walked it again to be sure.

quests.title: A guest who writes all night

opening.speaker: vlad
opening.text: Book my table for half past seven, if you please. My house guest from abroad has arrived. He is a polite young man, but he writes letters all night and burns my candles. Red wine and roast lamb. I must recover my patience.

completion.speaker: vlad
completion.text: Excellent. My guest asked whether the doors of my castle lock from the outside. I told him that every door locks from somewhere. He did not find that comforting.

opening.speaker: eszter
opening.text: I have built kilns, but never a clay oven for bread. Ilie says that it is the same thing, only hungrier.

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: And it needs patience.

opening.speaker: eszter
opening.text: I have patience. I do not have lunch. Bring a bulz and a cheese pie to the shed, and I will start the base.

completion.speaker: eszter
completion.text: The base is laid, and the dome is up. It must dry for three days, with a small fire each evening.

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: My great-grandmother would approve.

completion.speaker: eszter
completion.text: Your great-grandmother would complain about the straw. Your notebook says so on page four.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Sorin, show me the orchard. If it creaks, I want to hear it in daylight.

opening.speaker: sorin
opening.text: In daylight it only sighs. I will bring a basket. Nobody sighs at a picnic.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Pogăcele, plum jam, compote, and a cheese pie, then. A picnic by the fence.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: Thirty old trees, apples and plums, and a gate that a monk unlocks once a year. The notice on the gate gives the price.

completion.speaker: sorin
completion.text: It is a large number.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: It is a very large number. I am writing it in the notebook anyway.

opening.speaker: victor
opening.text: My exams start in June. I have read the anatomy book twice, and it has read me once. A linden tea, a meatball soup, and smoked cheese, please: for the nerves, the stomach, and the bones.

completion.speaker: victor
completion.text: I can name every muscle of the face now. I tried them all in the mirror. My landlady thinks that I am possessed. I am only revising.

quests.title: A hot night on the ward

opening.speaker: ana
opening.text: The night ward is as hot as a bread oven. The patients cannot sleep, and neither can the doctor. He keeps telling me that it is not a bread oven. A pogăcea, a linden tea, and a jar of cold zacuscă, please.

completion.speaker: ana
completion.text: I opened every window. A moth came in, then a bat, and then the doctor’s hat went out. Everyone is asleep now, even the hat.

opening.speaker: costel
opening.text: The summer festival needs music, so I am building a mechanical nightingale for the stage: brass, springs, and one small bellows. Papanași, a cheese pie, and a langoș, please. Small parts need a big lunch.

completion.speaker: costel
completion.text: The nightingale sings now. It sings only when it sees a shiny spoon, but it sings. I will polish a spoon for the festival.

opening.speaker: bran
opening.text: The town wants extra night buses in June: for the festival, and for Midsummer Eve. That is a lot of night. A langoș, a vegetable stew, and a bean soup in a bread bowl, please.

completion.speaker: bran
completion.text: I have planned the routes. The horse read the timetable over my shoulder. It did not like the part about the woods.

opening.speaker: sorin
opening.text: I have news from the town hall. The mayor wants a summer festival in the square on 21 June, and he wants food.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Which cook did he ask?

opening.speaker: sorin
opening.text: He asked me which cook to ask. I said your name with my mouth full of your langoș. He took it as a yes.

completion.speaker: sorin
completion.text: He will come himself to talk about the contract. He asked me if you are expensive.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: What did you say?

completion.speaker: sorin
completion.text: I said that you are worth it. He looked very sad.

opening.speaker: dorian
opening.text: I am giving a garden party. My roses are in bloom, my guests are in good health, and I am, as ever, unchanged. A cheese board and a cozonac, please. The guests bring the gossip.

completion.speaker: dorian
completion.text: A triumph. One guest asked for the name of my tailor, and another for the secret of my youth. I gave them both the same address.

opening.speaker: ana
opening.text: Everything on the hill is in flower, and the whole night ward sneezes. Even the skeleton in the teaching room. Do not ask how. A linden tea, a pogăcea, and a bean stew, please.

completion.speaker: ana
completion.text: The patients sneezed themselves to sleep. The skeleton is fine. I think that it was the draught in its ribs.

opening.speaker: elisabeta
opening.text: A table for half past seven, please. The count has moved the fence between our lands again, two metres to the east. Red wine and roast lamb. I shall plan my answer over dinner.

completion.speaker: elisabeta
completion.text: I have my answer. Tomorrow my men move the fence three metres to the west. Diplomacy is a matter of numbers.

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: The notebook says: “Bake when the oven stops talking.” The clay oven ticks and hisses all morning.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Maybe it never stops.

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: Then the bread waits for ever. Make me a loaf, a langoș, and some plum jam on the stove, and I will listen to the oven while I eat.

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: At noon it went quiet. I baked, and the crust burned on the left and stayed white on the right.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: Like the stove.

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: Like every oven in this family. I will turn the loaves halfway, and I will not write that in the notebook yet.

quests.title: The watch at the red door

opening.speaker: adrian
opening.text: We are back at the red door. We do not knock. We keep watch in turns, and we listen.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: To what?

opening.speaker: adrian
opening.text: To the snoring. It is louder this summer. We need food that keeps a watchman calm and a sleeper asleep: linden tea, heavy stews, and bread.

completion.speaker: adrian
completion.text: Packed. If the snoring stops, we come up at once. If it gets louder, we come up faster.

opening.speaker: bran
opening.text: The May rain finds every hole in the roof of my bus. Tonight I drive with an umbrella in one hand and the wheel in the other. A langoș, a bean soup in a bread bowl, and plum jam, please.

completion.speaker: bran
completion.text: Twelve passengers, eleven umbrellas, and one very wet horse. Everybody got home dry, except the horse and me.

opening.speaker: catalina
opening.text: On Thursday it is Ispas, the Ascension. I ring the bells at dawn, and the village hangs walnut leaves on the doors. Saramură with mămăligă, a plum dumpling, and a bean stew, please. Ringing is hungry work.

completion.speaker: catalina
completion.text: I rang until noon. A crow sat on the bell rope the whole time and swung with it. I have decided that it was helping.

opening.speaker: gavril
opening.text: The festival needs five stalls of food on 21 June, and the town budget is very small. Tochitură, mici, and papanași, please. I negotiate better after dessert, so I eat it first.

completion.speaker: gavril
completion.text: Agreed: five stalls, at the prices of the menu, paid after the festival. I wrote “after the festival” in very small letters. Please do not read them.

opening.speaker: victor
opening.text: One week to the exams. I revise all night by candlelight, and the candle revises with me. It is shorter every morning. A meatball soup, a linden tea, and a langoș, please.

completion.speaker: victor
completion.text: I passed the oral exam. The professor asked me what keeps a body alive. I said “soup”. He laughed for a long time and gave me a good mark.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: The first tomatoes are red. Four beds of seedlings, and these two came first.

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: In my family, the first tomato of summer is eaten with salt, standing in the garden.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Then we stand in the garden. Bring telemea, a langoș, and a cold socată.

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: Salt, tomato, cheese, and bread. Summer has started.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: And from now on, the beds feed the kitchen. Each vegetable that we grow ourselves is worth more on the menu.

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: Spoken like a farmer. Your grandmother would have charged double.

opening.speaker: eszter
opening.text: On the Saturday of the dead, families give a clay pot of food and a jug of water for each soul. Bela asked me for forty pots.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Forty?

opening.speaker: eszter
opening.text: He has many quiet neighbours. I throw pots all day, so bring food that I can eat with clay on my hands.

completion.speaker: eszter
completion.text: Forty pots, glazed and dry. Bela came for them before sunrise and thanked each pot by name.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: By name?

completion.speaker: eszter
completion.text: He names everything. My kiln is called Aunt Rozalia now.

opening.speaker: ileana
opening.text: The sleeves of a blouse carry the pattern of a village. I have stitched four villages so far, and I need three more by June. Stuffed peppers, plum jam, and zacuscă toast, please.

completion.speaker: ileana
completion.text: Seven villages are done. My brother says that one sleeve has a goat on it. It is a star. A star with horns.

opening.speaker: sanziana
opening.text: On Pentecost the Rusalii fly over the fields. They are wild fairies, and they dance a careless person into a fever. My sisters keep them away with wormwood. Wormwood wine, please, and food for after.

completion.speaker: sanziana
completion.text: Not one Rusalie came near us. My sisters danced in a ring with wormwood in their belts. Afterwards the wine was empty and the dumplings were gone. Nobody saw anyone eat.

opening.speaker: bela
opening.text: On Saturday the families give pots of food and water at the graves, in Eszter’s new pots. I keep the churchyard gate open from dawn, which is very early for me. A pogăcea, a linden tea, and a bean stew, please. I must stay awake through a whole sunny day.

completion.speaker: bela
completion.text: Forty pots at forty graves. The living ate together on the grass, and the dead were very well behaved. I slept from noon until the next evening.

opening.speaker: ana
opening.text: The old women say that the strigoi sleep in summer. I keep the garlic on the ward door anyway. Sleep is not the same as gone. A chicken noodle soup, a langoș, and a summer salad, please.

completion.speaker: ana
completion.text: Nothing knocked. A patient asked why the door smells of garlic in June. I told him that the door has a cold.

opening.speaker: costel
opening.text: The nightingale needs a perch for the stage. I am making a brass branch, and brass is stubborn. A cozonac, a langoș, and a bulz, please. I will be stubborn back.

completion.speaker: costel
completion.text: The branch is done, and the nightingale holds it with both feet. It sang twice when Sorin rode past. His bicycle bell is very shiny.

opening.speaker: sorin
opening.text: The mayor printed posters for the festival. I deliver them with the post, so every house gets one, and every dog chews one.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Every dog?

opening.speaker: sorin
opening.text: The posters are printed on very tasty paper. I need a lunch that I can eat faster than a dog.

completion.speaker: sorin
completion.text: Every house has a poster. Three dogs have two. The mayor’s dog ate the mayor’s copy, so he asked me for a new one.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: Did you give it to him?

completion.speaker: sorin
completion.text: He asked for a discount.

opening.speaker: bran
opening.text: On the festival night, the last bus leaves the square at two in the morning. I am testing the route. A bean soup in a bread bowl, a langoș, and an aubergine salad, please. The horse gets the bread bowl.

completion.speaker: bran
completion.text: The route is good. The bus took a short cut through the churchyard, but Bela waved us through.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: On Saturday we hold Mamaia’s six-month memorial. Six months, and I still reach for her notebook before my own.

opening.speaker: bela
opening.text: I have weeded her grave and mended its little fence. The roses there grow faster than any others. I do not ask why.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Colivă for the church, colaci for the gate, and her red wine for the priest.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: She always said that a priest should leave a memorial warmer than he came.

completion.speaker: bela
completion.text: Her grave had more flowers than the church. Half the village brought one, and the other half brought two.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: Everyone told me a story about her. Three of them were about a festival in this square, forty years ago.

completion.speaker: bela
completion.text: She cooked for that one too. History likes to repeat a good menu.

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: The clay oven still burns on the left. I tried everything in the notebook: wet straw, a brick, a prayer.

opening.speaker: eszter
opening.text: Did you try the other side of the oven?

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: There is no other side. There is only the left and the wrong side. A bread basket for the test, and something cold for the baker.

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: Eszter put a stone at the back. Now the oven bakes even on both sides.

completion.speaker: eszter
completion.text: It was a draught. Ovens are not mysterious.

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: Not in your family.

opening.speaker: victor
opening.text: The results go up on the board at the college tomorrow. I cannot sleep and I cannot eat, so I will eat to stop thinking. A meatball soup, a linden tea, and a tomato salad with telemea, please.

completion.speaker: victor
completion.text: I passed everything. The professor of anatomy wrote “unusual” on my paper. I think that it is a compliment. Now I have the whole summer for my project.

opening.speaker: dorian
opening.text: The painter wants summer light for my portrait. Summer light is honest, he says. I told him that I have nothing to fear from honesty. A cheese board and a fruit tea, please. Honesty makes me hungry.

completion.speaker: dorian
completion.text: The portrait is wonderful. In the summer light I look twenty-five. The painter looks ten years older than when he started. Sitting is hard work for everybody.

opening.speaker: elisabeta
opening.text: A table for half past seven, please. My men moved the fence three metres to the west, and the count has written me a letter in red ink. Very red. Red wine and roast pork. I shall reply in the same ink.

completion.speaker: elisabeta
completion.text: My reply is sealed. The count’s crows will carry it, if they ever stop circling my tower.

quests.title: The family comes for the festival

opening.speaker: mama
opening.text: We came on the morning bus for the festival. Your father brought his good shirt and his bad opinions.

opening.speaker: tata
opening.text: I have only good opinions. A village with a festival still has a future. The poster says so.

opening.speaker: mama
opening.text: Cook us Mamaia’s cabbage rolls, Mara. I want to taste them in her own kitchen.

completion.speaker: mama
completion.text: They are right. They taste of her kitchen, because it is her kitchen.

completion.speaker: tata
completion.text: I counted the people in the square. Two hundred, and every one of them knows your name.

completion.speaker: mama
completion.text: He will not say it, so I will. He is proud of you.

opening.speaker: eszter
opening.text: The mayor wants paper plates for the festival. Paper. In a village with a potter.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Paper is cheap.

opening.speaker: eszter
opening.text: Paper is sad. I will make two hundred small plates, and the mayor can pay for paper if he wants sadness.

opening.speaker: eszter
opening.text: Mici, a bulz, and a salad, please. I work better when I am angry and fed.

completion.speaker: eszter
completion.text: Two hundred plates. The mayor asked if they are free.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: Are they?

completion.speaker: eszter
completion.text: They are free to admire. They cost one coin to break.

opening.speaker: sanziana
opening.text: My sisters and I will make every garland for the square: bedstraw crowns, ropes of flowers, and a posy for each stall. We will not come to the festival. On Midsummer Eve we have our own night in the meadow. Food for the weaving, please. Many hands are hungry hands.

completion.speaker: sanziana
completion.text: The garlands are in your shed, and a letter is under the top one. On Midsummer Eve, girls throw their crowns onto a roof. A crown that stays on the roof means a wedding within the year. Choose your roof carefully.

opening.speaker: gavril
opening.text: The grill stall opens the festival. Mici and bread, and the smoke brings the people. Smoke is free advertising.

completion.speaker: gavril
completion.text: The grill is empty, the people are full, and my speech has not started. Next stall!

opening.speaker: gavril
opening.text: The bakery stall. Langoș for the grown-ups, chimney cakes for the children, and both for me, as the inspector.

completion.speaker: gavril
completion.text: Inspected and approved. Next stall!

opening.speaker: gavril
opening.text: The garden stall. People say that a festival has no vegetables. We will prove them wrong, gently.

completion.speaker: gavril
completion.text: Gone, even the salad. I have never seen people queue for salad. Next stall!

opening.speaker: gavril
opening.text: The drinks stall. Socată for the children and wormwood wine for the brave. I am brave in moderation.

completion.speaker: gavril
completion.text: Every glass is empty. The piper asked for a second wormwood wine, and then a third. Last stall!

painting.title: The festival
painting.text: The town square on the evening of 21 June, under Sânziana’s garlands. Tarka Miklós plays on the stage, and a line of rats follows his tune. Gavril Hămălescu makes a speech at the front. Mara works at the grill stall. Mama and Tata sit at a table, and Ilie, Eszter, and Sorin move between the stalls, in a crowd of villagers.

opening.speaker: gavril
opening.text: The sweets stall, and then my speech. A sweet end makes people forgive a long speech.

completion.speaker: gavril
completion.text: My speech lasted forty minutes. Nobody left, because the piper played under it.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: Your speech had a very good tune.

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: Look at the square, Mara. Every stall is empty, and every table is full.

opening.speaker: cezar
opening.text: Saturday is the shortest night of the year, and the festival keeps the whole village awake. I have almost no night to watch, and nobody to watch over. A tochitură and a bean soup, please. I will rest my eyes for both of us.

completion.speaker: cezar
completion.text: The night lasted six hours. I watched four of them. The other two watched me.

opening.speaker: sanziana
opening.text: It is almost Midsummer Eve. We dance until dawn, so we need plum dumplings and zacuscă. Dancing is hungry work.

completion.speaker: sanziana
completion.text: We danced until sunrise and wove a crown for you. It hangs on the gate. Do not wear it after dark.

opening.speaker: bran
opening.text: On Midsummer Eve the night bus goes through the woods to the meadow. The horse refuses. He stands at the edge of the trees and looks at me. A langoș, mici, and a tomato salad with telemea, please. I need a good argument.

completion.speaker: bran
completion.text: We went round the woods. It took an hour longer. In the meadow, girls danced in a ring that was a little too big for the number of girls. The horse was right.

opening.speaker: ileana
opening.text: On Tuesday the whole village wears the embroidered blouse. Eleven blouses are finished, and the twelfth is mine, which I have not started. Zacuscă toast, stuffed peppers, and an aubergine salad, please. I will sew through lunch.

completion.speaker: ileana
completion.text: I finished mine at midnight. The thread ran out on the last star, so it has a tail. Everybody says that it is a comet. I say so too.

opening.speaker: ana
opening.text: On Sânziene the medicinal herbs are at their strongest. I gather them at dawn, before the dew dries: yarrow, St John’s wort, and lime flowers. Two linden teas and a langoș, please. I will be out before the birds.

completion.speaker: ana
completion.text: A whole basket of herbs, enough for the ward until winter. A barefoot girl in a crown of bedstraw showed me the best patch. She said that her name was Sânziana. She did not look like the florist.

opening.speaker: gavril
opening.text: The festival was a great success, and great successes are expensive. The town budget is very sad. Tochitură, mici, and a socată, please. The budget and I need comfort.

completion.speaker: gavril
completion.text: The budget is closed, and the stalls are paid, as agreed. The piper is another matter. He wants coins. I offered him the glory of the town. He laughed at me.

opening.speaker: tarka
opening.text: Tarka Miklós, piper. I played at the festival, and the mayor paid me in compliments. Compliments are very thin. I cannot eat them.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Then the bistro pays you. What would you like?

opening.speaker: tarka
opening.text: Wormwood wine, mici, and a chimney cake. In return, I will play one tune for your cellar. Nobody refuses my tunes. Not even the rats.

completion.speaker: tarka
completion.text: Paid in full, and better than coins. Listen.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: That tune! The rats under the floor are walking out of the cellar door in a line.

completion.speaker: tarka
completion.text: They will come back. Rats always do. But for a month of Sundays, they will dance somewhere else. Farewell, Mara.

opening.speaker: eszter
opening.text: Eleven of my festival plates came back broken. The rest came back with names scratched on them.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Names?

opening.speaker: eszter
opening.text: People liked them so much that they signed them. I must decide whether this is vandalism or praise. Lunch first.

completion.speaker: eszter
completion.text: I have decided. It is praise. I will glaze over the names and sell the plates back to their owners.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: Is that fair?

completion.speaker: eszter
completion.text: It is business. The mayor taught me.

quests.title: A nightingale that will not stop

opening.speaker: costel
opening.text: Since the festival, my nightingale sings every night, with no spoon at all. It sings at the moon, at Cezar, and at my landlady. Two papanași and a bulz, please. I must learn to think like a bird.

completion.speaker: costel
completion.text: I found the trouble. It is in love with the weathervane of the church. I cannot repair love, so I have given it a good oil.

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: Mara, may I read Mamaia’s notebook beside mine? Our grandmothers cooked in the same village for fifty years.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Read it. Except the page in the old letters. Nobody can read that one.

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: I only want the recipes. Bring me something with this year’s tomatoes, and we will compare.

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: Her cabbage rolls and my grandmother’s are the same, except for one word: “patience” in mine, and “more pepper” in hers.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: And the strange page?

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: The letters are too even. My grandmother’s hand wobbled when she was angry. That page never wobbles.

opening.speaker: catalina
opening.text: Sorin says that a monk of the cathedral cannot sleep for the snoring. I have offered to ring him a lullaby. Saramură with mămăligă, a bean stew, and an aubergine salad, please. A lullaby on a bell needs strong arms.

completion.speaker: catalina
completion.text: I rang very softly, one stroke every minute. Half the village fell asleep in the street. The monk did not. He says that he will come to the bistro instead.

quests.title: The shelf of the torn book

opening.speaker: monica
opening.text: We found the library under the cathedral again. One shelf holds a book with a torn cover, and its pages are sewn back badly.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Who sewed it?

opening.speaker: monica
opening.text: Someone in a hurry, forty years ago. The librarian screams when we touch it. We need hot stews and bread for the watch while Janos argues with him.

completion.speaker: monica
completion.text: The stews are packed. If the librarian screams again, we will offer him a lamb stew. Everybody has a price.

opening.speaker: bela
opening.text: One grave in my churchyard hums in the evening: the old miller’s. He was a cheerful man, so I do not mind, but the bees are confused. A pogăcea, a linden tea, and a bulz, please.

completion.speaker: bela
completion.text: It was a beehive, inside the stone angel. The miller always loved honey. I have left them both alone.

opening.speaker: sorin
opening.text: On my round I met a monk from the cathedral. He walked very slowly, with his eyes half closed.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Tired?

opening.speaker: sorin
opening.text: He has not slept for a month. He says that the snoring under the cathedral comes up through his bed.

opening.speaker: sorin
opening.text: He asked me if the bistro has a quiet courtyard.

completion.speaker: sorin
completion.text: I told him yes. Then I remembered Miez, the bats, and Cezar.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: Ambrozie will manage. He is the monk who sells us the pickles.

completion.speaker: sorin
completion.text: You know him?

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: I know his pickles. That is half a man.

opening.speaker: ambrozie
opening.text: I am Ambrozie, a monk of the cathedral. I have not slept since Easter. Something under the cathedral snores, and the stones carry it into my cell.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Sorin said that you might come.

opening.speaker: ambrozie
opening.text: May I dine here on Saturday at half past seven, and sleep in your courtyard? I am told that your cat is quiet.

completion.speaker: ambrozie
completion.text: A stew without meat, as the brothers make it, only better. I will sleep under your walnut tree tonight.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: Miez sleeps on the roof of the summer kitchen. He may sing.

completion.speaker: ambrozie
completion.text: After a month of snoring, a singing cat is a lullaby.

opening.speaker: ambrozie
opening.text: Good morning. I slept nine hours. I am told that I snore too, and that your cat slept on the roof in protest.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: He came down for breakfast.

opening.speaker: ambrozie
opening.text: Then all is forgiven. Ilie says that you have a notebook with a page that nobody can read. Old pages are my trade.

completion.speaker: ambrozie
completion.text: This page is not handwritten. It is printed, with a red initial. It comes from a book of prayers in the library of the cathedral.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: Mamaia tore a page out of a church book?

completion.speaker: ambrozie
completion.text: And pasted it in, very neatly. It is a prayer against strigoi. I must go back and look at the shelf. Thank you for the lunch, and for the sleep.

quests.title: A cold place for the project

opening.speaker: victor
opening.text: My summer project must stay cold until the thunder comes, so I have borrowed the ice cellar of the college. It is very cold, and I am very hungry. A meatball soup, a linden tea, and a sharing board, please.

completion.speaker: victor
completion.text: The project is cold, and so am I. The porter asked what I keep in the ice cellar. I said “dessert”. He crossed himself.

opening.speaker: cezar
opening.text: The July moon is so bright that I see my own shadow at midnight. Last night my shadow walked one step behind me. Tonight I will walk faster. A tochitură, a bean soup, and mici, please.

completion.speaker: cezar
completion.text: My shadow kept up the whole night. We have agreed to walk together. It is good company, and it never asks for half of my supper.

opening.speaker: dorian
opening.text: An old friend from the city visits me this week. She has aged beautifully. I have not aged at all, which she finds rude. A cheese board and a socată, please. I must look a little tired for her sake.

completion.speaker: dorian
completion.text: I stayed up all night so that I would look tired. It did not work. She says that I look rested. Some gifts are a burden.

quests.title: A guest who sleeps all day

opening.speaker: vlad
opening.text: My table at half past seven, if you please. My house guest now sleeps all day and wanders all night. He says that it is the climate. Red wine, and meatballs in tomato sauce. The sauce is red. I find that restful.

completion.speaker: vlad
completion.text: Very good. My guest asked again about the trains. I told him that the next train leaves in the autumn. Probably.

opening.speaker: dorian
opening.text: It is so hot that my portrait in the attic has started to sweat. I have not. A glass of red wine, a cozonac, and a tomato salad with telemea, please. I shall stay cool, as usual.

completion.speaker: dorian
completion.text: I opened the attic window for the portrait. It looked out at the village for an hour, and then it turned its face to the wall. Some pictures do not like summer.

opening.speaker: cezar
opening.text: Somebody saw me asleep on the bench in the square at three in the morning. I was resting my eyes, and my eyes were snoring. A tochitură, mici, and a summer salad, please.

completion.speaker: cezar
completion.text: Tonight I walk the round twice: once for the village, and once for my reputation.

opening.speaker: eszter
opening.text: The hail broke half of my pots in the yard. Not the cheap ones. The best ones, of course.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: A tinker came to the square this morning, with wire and a bag of tools.

opening.speaker: eszter
opening.text: A tinker. Mending my pots with wire. My pride says no, and my shelves say yes. Feed me while they argue.

completion.speaker: eszter
completion.text: He sewed them with copper wire, like a coat. They hold water better than before.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: And your pride?

completion.speaker: eszter
completion.text: Mended too. I am keeping the mended pots for the feast. Broken and mended is a good story for a plate.

opening.speaker: catalina
opening.text: The first hail cloud came over the hill this morning before I reached the rope. It broke your pots, Mara, and I am sorry. The second cloud I rang away. My arms are hungry. Zacuscă toast and plum dumplings, please. It is a fasting day.

completion.speaker: catalina
completion.text: Not one more hailstone fell. The bell and I have agreed: next time we start at the first grey cloud. Maybe at the first grey goose.

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: Sunday is Saint Elijah, my name day. The whole village expects bread from me, all at once.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: The clay oven can do it.

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: The oven can do the bread. I cannot do the waiting. Make colaci and a bread basket for the first guests, and I will bake the rest.

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: Forty loaves, and thunder all afternoon, as is right for Saint Elijah. I wrote the summer recipes in the notebook, in my own hand.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: Your first new pages.

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: Mamaia’s notebook gave me courage. Every page of mine is handwritten. I checked.

opening.speaker: victor
opening.text: My summer project needs lightning, and Saint Elijah brings thunder. On Sunday I will put a copper rod on the roof of the college. Two meatball soups and a bean stew, please. I will need my strength for the climb.

completion.speaker: victor
completion.text: The lightning struck the rod at six o’clock. The project sat up, trembled, and rose. It was a soufflé again. It is the best soufflé that the college has ever seen.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Ambrozie sent a note from the cathedral. He found the book. Every page is there except one.

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: The one in Mamaia’s notebook.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: He will tell me the rest at the feast. Until then, I want to cook something that stops me thinking about it.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: I keep looking at the page. Mamaia pasted it in so carefully, as if she was ashamed and proud at the same time.

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: My grandmother kept a borrowed pan for thirty years. She said that she would return it when it was clean.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: Was it ever clean?

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: Never. Some things are not borrowed. They are kept.

opening.speaker: ileana
opening.text: My brother has left his spindle again, in July. Joimărița does not come in summer, so he thinks that he is safe. Fruit tea, zacuscă toast, and a monk’s stew, please. I will give him a lecture between bites.

completion.speaker: ileana
completion.text: He spun all afternoon. Then the wind blew the door shut, and he spun all evening. He thinks that it was Joimărița. I did not tell him that it was me.

opening.speaker: janos
opening.text: I have read the loose pages of the archbishop again. He wrote down the date of every sermon, and one date twice.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Which date?

opening.speaker: janos
opening.text: The night that a page left the library: the same year that he left the village with the money for the roof. We need hearty food for the last search.

completion.speaker: janos
completion.text: We go down once more. Then I can tell you everything at a proper meal, after the feast. I have not forgotten my promise.

opening.speaker: sanziana
opening.text: My sisters are having a picnic in the meadow. Roasted vegetables and zacuscă for two, and plum dumplings for the rest. I will not tell you how many the rest are.

completion.speaker: sanziana
completion.text: My sisters thank you, all of them. You may hear singing in the meadow tonight. Please do not go and count us.

opening.speaker: costel
opening.text: The weathervane of the church has turned to face my nightingale. It has not moved since Tuesday, whatever the wind does. Socată, papanași, and a tochitură, please. This is a mechanical romance, and I am responsible.

completion.speaker: costel
completion.text: I moved the nightingale to the other side of my shop. The weathervane followed it. I have decided to let love win, and to buy a barometer.

opening.speaker: elisabeta
opening.text: Half past seven, please, and not by the window. The count’s crows sit on my fence now. On both fences. Red wine, lamb chops, and a tomato salad with telemea.

completion.speaker: elisabeta
completion.text: I fed the crows some lamb. Now they sit on my side of the fence. The count will be furious. Excellent.

opening.speaker: mina
opening.text: Ionatan is my fiancé. He came from Britain to sign a property contract at the castle, but he has not written back. Have you seen him?

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: He had dinner here and left for the castle. He has not returned to the bistro.

opening.speaker: avram
opening.text: Then Mina and I will follow that road together. Before we leave, could you prepare a meal for two?

opening.speaker: mina
opening.text: No meat or fish, please. Eggs and dairy are fine.

completion.speaker: mina
completion.text: Thank you for the meal, and for telling us which road he took. We must find out why his letters stopped.

completion.speaker: avram
completion.text: We shall leave for the castle together now. I have my medical bag, should he need help.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: I hope that you find him safe. Take care on the road.

dialogue.speaker: sorin
dialogue.text: There is news going round the village. Mina and Doctor Avram found Ionatan gravely ill. All three have left for Britain. They did not stop at our bistro on the way back.

dialogue.speaker: mara
dialogue.text: Then he is no longer alone. I hope that he recovers at home. Thank you for bringing the news, Sorin.

opening.speaker: bran
opening.text: In August, half the village is at the seaside, and the other half wishes it was. My night bus is empty except for one pale gentleman who gets off at the castle. A langoș, a bean soup in a bread bowl, and a summer salad, please.

completion.speaker: bran
completion.text: He paid in very old coins and asked about the trains to the coast. I gave him the timetable. He thanked me without breathing.

opening.speaker: bela
opening.text: In August the families fast for two weeks, and then they all come to the graves for the Dormition. I am mending the paths before the crowd. A pogăcea, a linden tea, and a bean stew, please.

completion.speaker: bela
completion.text: The paths are mended, and every grave has a clean step. The old miller’s bees helped. They supervised.

opening.speaker: ileana
opening.text: Somebody borrowed a blouse from my shop on Midsummer Eve and brought it back in July, full of bedstraw. Zacuscă toast, stuffed peppers, and a bowl of bulion, please, while I pick out the flowers.

completion.speaker: ileana
completion.text: There was a crown of bedstraw in the sleeve, very small and very neat. I have kept it. Some customers pay in flowers.

opening.speaker: cezar
opening.text: At the end of July the dawn comes so early that my round ends before I start it. I asked the mayor for a longer night. He offered me a shorter round, for less money. A tochitură, a bean soup, and an aubergine salad, please.

completion.speaker: cezar
completion.text: I kept the long round and the same money. The mayor looked very pleased. I am not sure who won.

quests.title: A guest who left by the window

opening.speaker: vlad
opening.text: Half past seven, if you please. My house guest has left. Not by the door, which was open, but by the window, which was not. Young people have no manners. Red wine and roast pork, for my nerves.

completion.speaker: vlad
completion.text: The window is mended, and I have sent his luggage after him. I expect that someone will come for him. Someone always does.

opening.speaker: dorian
opening.text: The summer is ending, and my friends are going grey for the autumn. I have bought them hats. A cheese board and a fruit tea, please. Generosity is tiring.

completion.speaker: dorian
completion.text: They loved the hats. One friend asked why I never need one. I told her that I have a very good hatter in the attic.

quests.title: Half a ward in the fast

opening.speaker: ana
opening.text: Half of the ward keeps the Dormition fast, and the other half wants chicken soup. The kitchen of the clinic cooks only porridge. A chicken noodle soup, a linden tea, and a langoș, please, for the half that does not fast.

completion.speaker: ana
completion.text: The fasting half smelled the soup and confessed. The priest forgave them through the window. Everybody slept well.

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: Today is the Transfiguration. Fish is allowed, even in the fast. My grandmother called it the fish holiday of August.

opening.speaker: sorin
opening.text: She had a holiday for every fish?

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: Only for the important ones. Saramură, a monk’s stew, and colaci, please. I will write all three in the notebook.

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: Three new pages in my own hand: saramură for the Transfiguration, the monk’s stew of the fast, and colaci for every day after.

completion.speaker: sorin
completion.text: Will you put your name on them?

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: My granddaughter will. That is how notebooks work.

opening.speaker: sorin
opening.text: I have kept the secret of the page for a month, Mara. Do you know how hard that is for a man who carries the news?

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: You carry the post.

opening.speaker: sorin
opening.text: The post is mostly news. Yesterday I nearly told the baker, a goat, and the priest. Feed me, so that my mouth is busy.

completion.speaker: sorin
completion.text: Today the priest asked me what is new. I said, “The tomatoes.” Then I ran.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: Thank you, Sorin. After the feast, Ambrozie will tell everybody himself.

completion.speaker: sorin
completion.text: Then I will be the first to say that I knew. Quietly.

opening.speaker: cezar
opening.text: The feast of the cathedral brings people from three valleys, and three valleys of people means three valleys of lost hats. I will watch the square all night before the feast. A tochitură, a bean soup, and a summer salad, please.

completion.speaker: cezar
completion.text: I found eleven hats and one goat before dawn. The goat was wearing two of the hats.

opening.speaker: costel
opening.text: Cătălina asked me for a clock that counts the days of the fast. I built one that rings when the fast ends. It has rung three times already. Papanași, a bulz, and a monk’s stew, please. One of us is hungry.

completion.speaker: costel
completion.text: I found the trouble. The clock counted meals, not days. Now it counts days, and it sighs at every meal.

opening.speaker: bran
opening.text: For the feast of the cathedral, the town sends three buses of pilgrims. I drive the first. The horse drives nothing, but he insists on coming. A langoș, a monk’s stew, and mici, please.

completion.speaker: bran
completion.text: The pilgrims sang all the way, and the horse sang with them. Nobody had the heart to stop him.

opening.speaker: ana
opening.text: This week the whole ward fasts, even the doctor. He says that it is good for the heart. His heart says otherwise. A pogăcea, a linden tea, and a monk’s stew, please.

completion.speaker: ana
completion.text: The doctor ate the monk’s stew and declared it medicine. I am writing it on the chart of every patient.

opening.speaker: dorian
opening.text: The cathedral has invited me to the feast. I declined. Large crowds and old priests remember faces too well. A glass of red wine, a cheese pie, and a tomato salad with telemea, please. I shall feast quietly.

completion.speaker: dorian
completion.text: I shall watch the lights of the square from my window. My portrait wants to watch too. I have said no.

opening.speaker: eszter
opening.text: The head of the feast table needs ten plates. I have nine mended pots and one new plate.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Ten places, then.

opening.speaker: eszter
opening.text: Nine guests, and one chair for Mamaia. Her plate should be one of the mended ones. She would not want a new one.

completion.speaker: eszter
completion.text: Her plate is ready: the blue one with the copper stitches. It holds colivă better than any new plate.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: Thank you, Eszter.

completion.speaker: eszter
completion.text: Do not thank me. Thank the hail.

opening.speaker: ambrozie
opening.text: On the Dormition, the cathedral holds its feast in the square. This year I would like the bistro to cook it.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: For how many?

opening.speaker: ambrozie
opening.text: For those who know the story of the page: nine at the head of the table, and one chair for your grandmother. It is a fast with fish, so no meat, no milk, and no eggs.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Then Mamaia’s plate holds colivă and colaci, as at a memorial.

opening.speaker: catalina
opening.text: On the Dormition the big bell rings for the feast. It has not rung since Easter, and it is stiff. A plum dumpling and a fish soup, please. I will need both arms and a prayer.

completion.speaker: catalina
completion.text: It rang, and the whole valley heard it. Under the cathedral, something stopped snoring for a whole minute. Then it snored louder. I think that it liked the bell.

opening.speaker: bela
opening.text: On the Dormition the families bring food to the graves again, and I keep the gate open all day. I am not at the feast. My smile frightens the visiting priests. A linden tea and a colivă, please. The colivă is for the graves.

completion.speaker: bela
completion.text: Every grave had a visitor today. Mamaia’s had eleven. In the evening I sat with her for a while and told her about the feast. She seemed pleased.

opening.speaker: ileana
opening.text: The blouses are done, and now everybody wants a coat for the autumn. Coats are slower. Zacuscă toast, stuffed peppers, and a monk’s stew, please. Monks know about long work.

completion.speaker: ileana
completion.text: Twelve coats are cut. My brother does the buttons again. He has a new way to count them: he eats a plum for each one.

opening.speaker: costel
opening.text: My new barometer says “storm” when the nightingale sings and “fair” when it sleeps. I think that they are in love too. A cozonac and a bread basket, please. My shop is getting very romantic.

completion.speaker: costel
