completion.text: I have accepted it. The barometer, the nightingale, and the weathervane forecast the weather together now. They are wrong together, which is better than wrong alone.

opening.speaker: victor
opening.text: The autumn term starts in two weeks, and my soufflé has started to follow me to the library. It sits on the desk and rises when I read about the heart. A meatball soup, a linden tea, and a tomato salad with telemea, please.

completion.speaker: victor
completion.text: The professor has seen the soufflé. He wants to write a paper about it. The soufflé wants to be the first author.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: On Sunday the cathedral sells the orchard. I count the coins every night, and every night the number is the same.

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: Count them in the morning. Coins are braver in daylight.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Plum jam, pogăcele, compote, and a stew. Fruit from somebody else’s trees, for now.

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: Ambrozie says that the orchard money will finish the roof of the cathedral.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: Then the orchard pays the old debt too. Mamaia would like that.

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: She would ask for a discount first.

opening.speaker: sorin
opening.text: I walked past the orchard gate tonight. The trees were quiet. Not one creak.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Maybe they are waiting.

opening.speaker: sorin
opening.text: Maybe they heard that you are coming. A langoș, a bean stew, and a cherry compote, please. I will sit on the gate and listen.

completion.speaker: sorin
completion.text: At midnight, one tree creaked once. Very politely.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: A greeting?

completion.speaker: sorin
completion.text: Or a question. Trees are hard to read.

opening.speaker: janos
opening.text: I promised you a proper meal and the whole story. Ambrozie told the story at the feast, so I still owe you the meal.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Then sit down, Janos. Adrian and Monica too.

opening.speaker: janos
opening.text: Tochitură, cabbage rolls with mămăligă, meatballs in tomato sauce, cozonac, and a wormwood wine. Then I will tell you what the archbishop wrote about your grandmother. She is in his pages twice.

completion.speaker: janos
completion.text: Once as “the cook who would not pay the tithe”, and once as “the woman who reads at night in my library”. He was afraid of her.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: Good.

completion.speaker: janos
completion.text: We go back to the red door tomorrow. The sleeper is quieter since the bell. We will keep watch, and we will come back for your autumn menu.

opening.speaker: ambrozie
opening.text: The chronicle of the cathedral says that the sleeper behind the red door wakes every forty years, on All Hallows’ Eve, and asks for a feast.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: And forty years ago?

opening.speaker: ambrozie
opening.text: Forty years ago nobody cooked it. This year the debt of the page is paid in service, so the bistro cooks. The library kept his old menus. Here is the first scroll: the cold table.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Then I cook it. Who carries it down?

completion.speaker: adrian
completion.text: The cold table waits on a shelf in the cellar under the cathedral, by the red door. Nothing spoils down there: the cold keeps a sausage until spring.

completion.speaker: monica
completion.text: While we unpacked, the snoring stopped. Then it started again, a little happier.

completion.speaker: janos
completion.text: The archbishop still preaches to the door. He asked if he is invited. Ambrozie says that he can wash the pots.

opening.speaker: sorin
opening.text: Mara, something sleeps behind the red door and wakes on All Hallows’ Eve. I carry the news of this village. I want to see it first.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Nobody sees it, Sorin. We cook for it.

opening.speaker: sorin
opening.text: Then I see it first and cook for it second. Feed me while I make a plan.

completion.speaker: sorin
completion.text: I asked Adrian to take me down. He said no. I asked Monica. She said no, very slowly.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: And Janos?

completion.speaker: sorin
completion.text: Janos said no in three languages. I will find a fourth.

opening.speaker: gavril
opening.text: The deed of the orchard is ready: one page, three stamps, and a tax that I invented this morning. Mici and two plates of beans with sausages, please. A signature is hungry work for a mayor.

completion.speaker: gavril
completion.text: Signed and stamped. The tax is one basket of apples a year, for the town hall. I shall collect it personally, with a large basket.

opening.speaker: victor
opening.text: The new term has started, and the professor wants a skeleton for the lecture hall. The college sent me to the churchyard with a letter. Bela read it and laughed for an hour. A meatball soup, zacuscă toast, and a sharing board, please, while my dignity recovers.

completion.speaker: victor
completion.text: Bela lent me a plaster skeleton from the church storeroom. It wears a hat. The professor has asked no questions.

opening.speaker: dorian
opening.text: Forty years ago I dined in this bistro on All Hallows’ Eve. I remember the date, because that night something ate my dessert. A cheese board and a glass of red wine, please. I shall tell you the rest when I feel brave.

completion.speaker: dorian
completion.text: Your grandmother served that night. She said that the dessert walked away. I said that desserts do not walk. We were both a little right.

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: This summer I wrote my first recipes in my own hand. This autumn I want to try them: a cellar full of my own jars.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: The cellar is full of dust.

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: Then the jars wait, and I write.

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: Eleven recipes. Plums in honey, peppers in oil, cabbage my way, and eight more.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: Your grandmother’s way?

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: Mine. She would argue with every page. That is how I know they are good.

opening.speaker: vlad
opening.text: Eight o’clock, if you please. The hunting season opens, and I have caught nothing for three centuries. Decades. I misspoke. Red wine and roast veal, and a table far from the window.

completion.speaker: vlad
completion.text: The hunt was a success. I caught a cold. Your roast veal was better than the deer that I did not catch.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Our first apples. In August I said I would keep paying. Ambrozie says this dinner pays the page and frees the family. It must be perfect.

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: Perfect is a big word for a cook.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Then I start to practise now. Taste everything, and be honest.

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: The apples are sour, the pie and the tochitură are good, the langoș is perfect, and the soup needs salt.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: That is not perfect.

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: It is September. You have until All Hallows’ Eve.

opening.speaker: ambrozie
opening.text: The second scroll: the soups of the old feasts. Hot enough to wake a bishop, and gentle enough for a sleeper.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Is the menu the same as forty years ago?

opening.speaker: ambrozie
opening.text: The same as four hundred years ago. He is a creature of habit, like every monk that I know.

completion.speaker: monica
completion.text: The soups are on the shelf by the red door. We kept them warm with a blanket and a prayer.

completion.speaker: janos
completion.text: On our way up, the snoring changed its rhythm. I think that he counts the courses.

opening.speaker: sanziana
opening.text: Sunday is Holy Cross Day. The village takes basil to the church for the blessing, and my sisters and I pick the last herbs of the year. It is a long day of picking, so we need food for all of us.

completion.speaker: sanziana
completion.text: The basil is blessed, and the herbs hang in bunches. On Holy Cross Day the snakes go under the ground to sleep for the winter, and a grass snake nodded to us on its way. Everything goes to sleep now. Almost everything.

opening.speaker: adrian
opening.text: The last watch at the red door starts now. Ambrozie wants somebody awake by the door every night until All Hallows’ Eve.

opening.speaker: sorin
opening.text: I could take a night.

opening.speaker: adrian
opening.text: No. We need food for many nights, and calm food. Nothing that excites the stomach, ours or his.

completion.speaker: adrian
completion.text: The watch is set, and Monica takes the first night. If you hear a knock from below, it is only us. If you hear a knock from below while we are up here, do not open.

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: The cellar is clean, the barrels smell of oak, and my recipes are ready. Today I fill the first jars for winter.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: All of them today?

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: All of them, in my own order.

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: Thirty jars, full and labelled. The cellar smells like my grandmother’s.

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: One label says “Do not open before winter”. I did not write that one.

opening.speaker: bela
opening.text: Long ago, when I was a young gravedigger, I worked late. On the All Hallows’ Eve of the raid I sat on the churchyard wall and watched the village. I have never told anybody what I saw. Feed me first. It is a long story for an empty stomach.

completion.speaker: bela
completion.text: At midnight the pantry doors of the village opened, one after another, all the way down the hill. No lamp, no hand. Only the doors. Every door but one: your grandmother’s stayed shut. In the morning every other pantry was empty, and every door was closed again.

opening.speaker: eszter
opening.text: The old kitchen under the cathedral has a long table for forty, Ambrozie says. The cathedral deserves a table to be proud of.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: The cathedral, or the sleeper?

opening.speaker: eszter
opening.text: The table. I do not set a table that I am ashamed of, for anybody. Feed me, and I will draw the plates.

completion.speaker: eszter
completion.text: A plate and a cup at every place, and a jug at each end.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: He eats alone, Eszter.

completion.speaker: eszter
completion.text: Then he eats alone at a proper table.

opening.speaker: elisabeta
opening.text: At eight o’clock, please. My vineyard is harvested, and the count claims half of the grapes, because his crows ate them. Red wine, veal stew, and roast lamb. I need my strength for the lawyers.

completion.speaker: elisabeta
completion.text: The lawyers agree that the crows owe me the grapes. The count has offered to pay in crows.

opening.speaker: ambrozie
opening.text: The third scroll: the birds, the fish, and the meatballs of the old feasts. And at the bottom, plum brandy, underlined twice.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: For a sleeper?

opening.speaker: ambrozie
opening.text: For his digestion. The scroll is very clear about his digestion.

completion.speaker: janos
completion.text: We carried the third course through the open gate and set it on the long table in the dust of the kitchen.

completion.speaker: adrian
completion.text: A mouse came to look. It saw the plum brandy and left at once.

opening.speaker: monica
opening.text: The watch goes well. Adrian sleeps through his nights, Janos reads through his, and I listen.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: To what?

opening.speaker: monica
opening.text: To the dust. Under the cathedral, the dust moves on its own, very slowly, towards the red door. We need hot meals for the long nights.

completion.speaker: monica
completion.text: Packed. Janos says that the dust moves only in a draught. Janos also reads with his staff in his hand.

opening.speaker: costel
opening.text: I built a clock that measures the snoring under the cathedral. Each snore moves the hand one minute. The clock now says Thursday of next year. A papanași, zacuscă toast, and a sharing board, please, while I repair the future.

completion.speaker: costel
completion.text: I moved the clock to your cellar, far from the snoring. Now it keeps perfect time, and it ticks very quietly, so that nobody wakes.

opening.speaker: eszter
opening.text: I made the first plate for the sleeper. The best clay, three glazes, two firings. I carried it down to the long table myself.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: And?

opening.speaker: eszter
opening.text: He snored once, and it cracked from rim to rim. I need lunch, and then I need to think.

completion.speaker: eszter
completion.text: A plate that cracks at one snore is not a plate. It is a suggestion.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: So you make a stronger one?

completion.speaker: eszter
completion.text: I make a bigger one. Much bigger. And I mend the rims before he can crack them.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: The old women of the village keep a loaf hidden behind the flour sack, every autumn. Since the night of the raid.

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: My mother too. Behind the flour, wrapped in a towel.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Forty years of spare loaves. Then this village was more frightened than anybody says.

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: I asked my mother why. She said: “So that he finds something, and leaves the rest.”

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: This year he finds a whole dinner. Then the loaves can come out from behind the flour.

opening.speaker: dorian
opening.text: On the night of the raid, your grandmother served me an apple strudel. I turned to pour the wine. When I turned back, the plate was clean, and the curtains were moving. I have not eaten strudel since. Today I am ready to try again.

completion.speaker: dorian
completion.text: Your grandmother’s prayer kept her pantry shut. It did not cover my plate. This time I kept one hand on it, and nothing walked away. I am very relieved, and a little disappointed.

opening.speaker: sorin
opening.text: I asked Ambrozie if I can carry a course down the stairs. He said no. I asked the priest. He said no and blessed me.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Everybody says no, Sorin.

opening.speaker: sorin
opening.text: Everybody says no to me. And this morning the baker told me about the scrolls. My own secret, Mara, from a baker.

completion.speaker: sorin
completion.text: I kept the secret for a whole month. The whole village kept it with me.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: Then it is the best-kept secret in the village.

completion.speaker: sorin
completion.text: It is the only one. I checked.

opening.speaker: cezar
opening.text: On the night of the raid, the night watchman was my uncle. On All Hallows’ Eve he walked the village all night and saw nothing. He says that he was resting his eyes. It runs in the family. A sharing board, a bean soup in a bread bowl, and mici, please.

completion.speaker: cezar
completion.text: My uncle says that this year I must keep my eyes open. I have bought coffee. A lot of coffee.

opening.speaker: ambrozie
opening.text: The fourth scroll, and the heaviest: the roasts.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: How many roasts?

opening.speaker: ambrozie
opening.text: Two of each animal that the scroll can spell. The brother who wrote it was not a good speller, so there are only three kinds.

completion.speaker: adrian
completion.text: The roasts are on the long table under the cathedral. The hearth is lit now, and the whole hall smells of a feast.

completion.speaker: monica
completion.text: Behind the red door, something sniffed. A long, polite sniff.

opening.speaker: janos
opening.text: The watch ends on All Hallows’ Eve. I have read the whole chronicle by the red door, and I know the end of the story.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Tell me.

opening.speaker: janos
opening.text: He eats, he says a few words, and he sleeps for forty years. The chronicle does not say which words. We need suppers for the last nights.

completion.speaker: janos
completion.text: The last suppers are packed. If the chronicle is right, we have nothing to fear. If the chronicle is wrong, we have good food.

opening.speaker: bela
opening.text: I have counted the pantries of the village. In the year of the raid there were sixty-one. This year there are seventy-two, and every one has a new lock. Locks will not help. A linden tea, beans with sausages, and a bread basket, please.

completion.speaker: bela
completion.text: I told the families: lock your pantries if you like, but this year the bistro feeds him. Three families took the locks off. Two put on a second lock. One family left a cake.

opening.speaker: sorin
opening.text: Last night I went down the stairs under the cathedral. Alone. With a candle.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Sorin!

opening.speaker: sorin
opening.text: I got halfway. Then the snoring came up the stairs and blew out my candle. I need a hot meal and a lot of courage, in that order.

completion.speaker: sorin
completion.text: I will not go down again. The red door can keep its secret.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: Good.

completion.speaker: sorin
completion.text: And I can keep mine. I did not tell anybody that I went. Except you. And the candle.

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: I took my jars to the market. Everybody smelled them, everybody liked them, and everybody bought the pickles of the cathedral.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: People trust what they know.

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: People trust a monk with a barrel. I am only a baker with a jar. Feed the baker.

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: Ambrozie came to the market and tasted my peppers. He said nothing.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: Nothing at all?

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: He took a second pepper. For a monk, that is a speech.

opening.speaker: bran
opening.text: The town has a pumpkin fair this weekend. Last year I carved the best pumpkin head. People said that I understand heads very well. A langoș, a vegetable stew, and a bean soup in a bread bowl, please.

completion.speaker: bran
completion.text: The langoș is for the bus. The rest is for me. The pumpkin head is for anyone who needs one.

opening.speaker: vlad
opening.text: Eight o’clock, if you please. My castle is cold in October, and the fireplace has forgotten how to burn. Red wine, roast lamb, and roast pork, near your warm stove.

completion.speaker: vlad
completion.text: I have borrowed your recipe for warmth. I shall serve it to my guests. I have no guests, but I am an optimist.

opening.speaker: dorian
opening.text: My portrait in the attic was painted the week after the raid. The painter put a crumb of apple strudel in its corner, as a memento, and the portrait has looked hungry ever since. A cheese board, a cozonac, and baked apples, please. I shall eat for both of us.

completion.speaker: dorian
completion.text: I told the portrait about this year’s dinner. It looked relieved. Then it looked older. It always does.

opening.speaker: ambrozie
opening.text: The fifth scroll: the great wooden platter and the slow roasts. The old brothers called it the course of the patient guest.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Why patient?

opening.speaker: ambrozie
opening.text: It takes three hours to cook. He has waited forty years. Three hours is nothing.

completion.speaker: monica
completion.text: Everything went down on our shoulders. The stairs creaked at every step.

completion.speaker: janos
completion.text: The hall is warm now, Mara. In the firelight, it looks like a church on a feast day.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Tuesday is Saint Parascheva, Mamaia’s name day. She always baked colaci for the neighbours and kept the last one for herself.

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: And a glass of wine for the saint.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: This year I cook a dinner for the thing that she stole a prayer to keep out. I want to bake her colaci, and ask her what she thinks.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: I put a colac on her chair and a glass of wine beside it.

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: And what does she think?

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: She thinks that I worry too much. She always did.

opening.speaker: eszter
opening.text: I have mended every plate in the cupboard of the cathedral. Copper on the rims, so that they do not crack.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: And the sleeper’s plate?

opening.speaker: eszter
opening.text: His plate is still in my head. It is too big for my kiln, and for my head. I will measure again.

completion.speaker: eszter
completion.text: I measured the long table, the hearth, and the door. The plate goes through the door if we roll it on its edge.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: Like a wheel?

completion.speaker: eszter
completion.text: Like a cartwheel. Thank you, Mara. That is exactly the size.

opening.speaker: ana
opening.text: My old patients ask for a loaf under the pillow, “for the night”. I told them that the bistro feeds everybody this year. They do not believe me. A chicken noodle soup, a bread basket, and baked apples, please. The bread is for the pillows.

completion.speaker: ana
completion.text: I brought them baked apples from your orchard. They ate them and slept like children. One still keeps a loaf under his pillow. He says that it is for me.

opening.speaker: dorian
opening.text: I hear that the sleeper dines alone this year. We are old acquaintances, he and I, although we were never introduced. A red wine and a cheese board, please. I shall drink to him, from a safe distance.

completion.speaker: dorian
completion.text: I shall spend All Hallows’ Eve at home, with my portrait and a strudel. We have both decided to keep one hand on the plate.

opening.speaker: ileana
opening.text: Ambrozie has ordered three aprons for a dinner under the cathedral: one for a guard, one for a pathfinder, and one for a scholar. He did not tell me who wears them, so I measured by guessing. Zacuscă toast, a bean soup in a bread bowl, and beans with sausages, please.

completion.speaker: ileana
completion.text: The aprons are done: plain linen with a red border and deep pockets. Janos asked for a pocket for a book. I gave him two.

opening.speaker: elisabeta
opening.text: Eight o’clock, please. The evenings are long now, and I read my estate papers by candlelight. The count reads them too, through my window. Red wine, roast lamb, and a tochitură, and a seat with my back to the wall.

completion.speaker: elisabeta
completion.text: I have moved my desk. Now the count reads my shopping list. Let him. It says “garlic”.

opening.speaker: ambrozie
opening.text: The sixth scroll is the last: the dinner itself, served at his chair on All Hallows’ Eve, at eight o’clock.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: And at the head of it?

opening.speaker: ambrozie
opening.text: A suckling pig with an apple in its mouth. The old menu draws it in the margin, with a smile.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Then the bistro cooks it, and this time we carry it down ourselves.

opening.speaker: eszter
opening.text: The plate is finished. It is the size of a cartwheel, with copper on every seam, and it took three kilns.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Three?

opening.speaker: eszter
opening.text: I fired it in pieces and mended it whole. A mended plate does not crack twice. Help me roll it to the cathedral.

completion.speaker: eszter
completion.text: It stands at his chair now. I signed it on the back.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: Why on the back?

completion.speaker: eszter
completion.text: So that he sees the food, and I see my name when he lifts it. He will lift it. Everybody lifts my plates.

opening.speaker: catalina
opening.text: All Hallows’ Eve is a Friday. A Friday! And the menu of the cathedral is roasts and brandy. Ambrozie says that the sleeper keeps his own calendar. I ring the bells by the church calendar, and so does my stomach. Saramură with mămăligă, a bean stew, and a fruit tea, please.

completion.speaker: catalina
completion.text: I asked the priest. He says that a fast is for people, and that the sleeper is not people. I will ring the bell for the dinner anyway. Quietly.

quests.title: The autumn Saturday of the dead

opening.speaker: bela
opening.text: On the autumn Saturday of the dead, the families bring colivă to the graves. Since the year of the raid, half the village stays home that day instead, to guard the pantry. A colivă, a linden tea, and a bean soup in a bread bowl, please.

completion.speaker: bela
completion.text: This year the families came to the graves, and the pantries stayed unguarded. Mamaia’s grave had a colac and a jar of peppers. I think that Ilie came early.

opening.speaker: dochia
opening.text: On Sunday it is Sâmedru, and the shepherds come down from the mountains. So do I. I left in March with nine sheepskins and came back with eleven. The flock is in the fold, the shepherds are hungry, and so is the dog. Food for all of us, please.

completion.speaker: dochia
completion.text: The shepherds have eaten, the dog has eaten, and the flock watched. They say that something under the cathedral snored all the way up to the high pasture this summer. The sheep did not mind. Sheep never mind.

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: The cold room is closed and cold, and my jars fill every shelf. The bistro keeps its own pickles now.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: And the barrels of the cathedral?

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: Ambrozie walked along the shelves twice and asked the price of a jar. A monk who asks a price wants to buy.

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: He bought a jar of peppers in oil and paid the full price. He did not ask for a discount.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: Mamaia would have asked for one.

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: And she would not have got one. I keep my own cellar now.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Since the feast I have crossed off a day in the notebook every night. One page, one dinner, and the debt is paid.

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: And now?

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Now I think that Mamaia never counted. She fed whoever came to the door, and she fed them well.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Tonight I cook for us, as she did. On Friday I cook for him the same way.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: On Friday I carry the pig to his chair myself.

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: Not Adrian? He has the arms for it.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: Adrian has the arms. I have the recipe. A host carries the best dish to the table.

opening.speaker: sorin
opening.text: Mara, on Friday the visitors serve at the long table, and Ambrozie stands at its end. Where do I stand?

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: In the kitchen, with Ilie and Eszter. With the trays.

opening.speaker: sorin
opening.text: The kitchen has a door. And a door has a crack. I accept.

completion.speaker: sorin
completion.text: I have oiled the hinges of the kitchen door. It opens without a sound now. Only a crack.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: Sorin.

completion.speaker: sorin
completion.text: For the trays, Mara. Only for the trays.

opening.speaker: sorin
opening.text: The kitchen is quiet for a moment. Mara says that the staff eat when the kitchen is quiet. Two loaves and two socată, and we sit down for once.

opening.speaker: bela
opening.text: The graves send their regards. Mămăligă and a hot linden tea, please, before the night gets cold.

opening.speaker: cezar
opening.text: My round starts soon. My feet already know the way, but my stomach does not. A bean soup and a loaf, please.

opening.speaker: ana
opening.text: Pickles keep the night nurses awake. Nobody can sleep with a mouth full of pickle. A pogăcea and mixed pickles, please.

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: A plain bowl for a fasting man, please: green beans, mămăligă, and a socată. My grandmother would call it a feast.

opening.speaker: victor
opening.text: I read that nettles are good for the nerves. Mine have an exam on Friday. A nettle soup, a loaf, and a linden tea, please.

opening.speaker: costel
opening.text: The church clock wants winding again, and the tower stairs are long. A linden tea, a fruit tea, and a slice of cozonac, please: one tea for me and one for the clock. I drink both.

opening.speaker: cezar
opening.text: Tonight is the longest night of the year, and I walk all of it. Tochitură, bean soup, and a sharing board, please. One bite for every hour.

completion.speaker: cezar
completion.text: The sun came up at last. I counted fourteen hours, two owls, and one shadow that walked home with me. It was polite.

opening.speaker: ana
opening.text: Tonight is Saint Andrew’s Eve. I will hang the garlic early, and then I want a proper supper: smoked cheese, a langoș, and a linden tea.

completion.speaker: ana
completion.text: The garlic is up and the plates are clean. Let anything knock tonight. We are fed, and we smell of garlic.

events.title: The funeral meal
events.line: Cook the funeral meal (pomană) for Mamaia Paraschiva, in the village. It is a fasting day.

scene.text: The village churchyard in snow. Mourners with candles stand before the church, among them Mara, Ilie, Eszter, and Sorin, beside a table with colivă and colaci.

opening.speaker: mama
opening.text: The colivă and the colaci are ready. Put them on the tray for the priest. He blesses them before anyone eats.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: The mourners come in from the cold churchyard. A bean dip for the fasting table, with plenty of garlic. Mamaia said that garlic keeps out the cold, and other things too.

dialogue.speaker: mara
dialogue.text: The telephone rang on Friday, on Saint Ignatius. Mamaia Paraschiva died in her sleep, in the village, in the house above her old bistro.

dialogue.speaker: mama
dialogue.text: She was ninety-one, and she still made her own colivă. She said that a colivă from a shop has no memory.

dialogue.speaker: mama
dialogue.text: The funeral is on Monday. We cook here in the city and drive it to the village. Colivă and colaci for the table of the dead, and beans, because it is a fasting day.

dialogue.speaker: mara
dialogue.text: I have not been to the village since I was twelve.

dialogue.speaker: mama
dialogue.text: Then the village has not seen you since you were twelve. Wash your hands.

dialogue.speaker: mara
dialogue.text: After the meal, I walked down to the bistro. The shutters are closed, and the sign has lost two letters.

dialogue.speaker: mara
dialogue.text: A black cat sat on the steps, as if he waited for the door to open.

dialogue.speaker: mama
dialogue.text: That is Miez. He was your grandmother’s. Nobody knows how old he is. She did not know either.

dialogue.speaker: mara
dialogue.text: When we packed the car, he was in my bag. He did not ask.

dialogue.speaker: mama
dialogue.text: Then he comes with us. A cat that chooses a bag has chosen a family.

events.title: Christmas Eve
events.line: Cook for the carol singers and the table of Christmas Eve. It is a fasting day.

scene.text: Three children with a paper star sing carols at the door of the flat. Tata holds out a basket of colaci, and Miez peeks out behind his legs.

opening.speaker: tata
opening.text: Every child who sings at our door gets a colac. That is the custom. I would like the custom to sing a longer song.

opening.speaker: mama
opening.text: Turte with honey and walnuts, as my mother made them. Thin enough to read the newspaper through, she said.

dialogue.speaker: tata
dialogue.text: The carol singers come tonight. I have counted the children in our block. Eleven, and the boy on the fourth floor counts as two.

dialogue.speaker: mama
dialogue.text: Then we need colaci for the door and turte for the table. It is still a fasting day.

dialogue.speaker: mara
dialogue.text: Miez is asleep on the radiator. He has not moved since we came home.

dialogue.speaker: tata
dialogue.text: A sensible animal.

dialogue.speaker: tata
dialogue.text: They sang three lines and held out their hands. When I was a boy, a carol had eleven verses, and a dog chased you after the fourth.

dialogue.speaker: mama
dialogue.text: You gave each of them two colaci.

dialogue.speaker: tata
dialogue.text: They sang the three lines very well.

dialogue.speaker: mara
dialogue.text: One small girl saw Miez on the windowsill and crossed herself. Then she asked for a colac for him too.

events.title: Christmas dinner
events.line: Cook Mamaia’s cabbage rolls from her notebook for Christmas dinner.

scene.text: Three children with a paper star sing carols at the door of the flat. Tata holds out a basket of colaci, and Miez peeks out behind his legs.

opening.speaker: mama
opening.text: Two pots of cabbage rolls from the notebook, word for word. If she wrote "a little", we use a little.

opening.speaker: tata
opening.text: The fast is over. I want a sausage, a slice of cozonac, and then a long nap.

dialogue.speaker: mama
dialogue.text: I brought your grandmother’s notebook from her kitchen drawer. Her cabbage rolls are on the first page.

dialogue.speaker: mara
dialogue.text: Listen: "Sour cabbage from the barrel, never from the shop. Roll them tight, like a child in winter. Cook them until the house smells of them, then one hour more."

dialogue.speaker: mara
dialogue.text: The page beside it is in letters that I cannot read. They look like the letters in old church books.

dialogue.speaker: tata
dialogue.text: That is the old writing. My grandfather could read it. He said it was mostly about the weather.

dialogue.speaker: mama
dialogue.text: Today we cook the cabbage rolls. The weather can wait.

page.text: Mamaia’s notebook, open at the cabbage rolls. The left page has the recipe in faded handwriting, a small drawing of a roll, and a grease stain. The right page has nine lines of old Cyrillic letters under a small red cross.

dialogue.speaker: mama
dialogue.text: They are good. They are nearly right.

dialogue.speaker: tata
dialogue.text: They are very good.

dialogue.speaker: mama
dialogue.text: Nearly. Something is missing, and the notebook does not say what.

dialogue.speaker: mara
dialogue.text: Maybe it is on the page that nobody can read.

events.title: New Year’s Eve
events.line: Cook the midnight table of New Year’s Eve.

scene.text: Mara, Mama, and Tata at the midnight table in the family kitchen, under paper streamers, with frost on the window and Miez on the windowsill. Tata raises his glass, and Mama says nothing.

opening.speaker: mama
opening.text: Two stuffed peppers. Your father eats the second one and says that it is for the old year.

opening.speaker: tata
opening.text: Sausages, and pickles from the barrel on the balcony. That barrel is the only thing in this flat that improves with age.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Papanași for midnight. If we eat them while the clock strikes, the year starts sweet.

opening.title: The last night of the year

dialogue.speaker: tata
dialogue.text: Stuffed peppers, sausages, pickles from the balcony, and papanași at midnight. That is a New Year’s table.

dialogue.speaker: mara
dialogue.text: And a long talk about the bistro, I suppose.

dialogue.speaker: tata
dialogue.text: After the papanași. Nobody makes a good decision before dessert.

dialogue.speaker: tata
dialogue.text: The building in the village is old, Mara. The roof leaks, and the village is far away. A man from the town has already asked to buy it.

dialogue.speaker: mara
dialogue.text: Mamaia kept it open for fifty years.

dialogue.speaker: tata
dialogue.text: And for the last ten, it was open only for the cat.

dialogue.speaker: mara
dialogue.text: Mama did not say a word. In our family, that is the loudest answer.

dialogue.speaker: tata
dialogue.text: Happy New Year, everyone.

events.title: Epiphany
events.line: Cook a warm meal for the priest who blesses the flat on Epiphany (Boboteaza).

scene.text: Mara, Mama, and Tata at the midnight table in the family kitchen, under paper streamers, with frost on the window and Miez on the windowsill. Tata raises his glass, and Mama says nothing.

opening.speaker: tata
opening.text: The priest climbs eight floors with his basil and his holy water. He gets a chicken soup, and I get one for the stairs that I did not climb. And a linden tea for his voice.

dialogue.speaker: mama
dialogue.text: The priest comes today to bless the flat. Your father has hidden the plum brandy.

dialogue.speaker: tata
dialogue.text: Behind the holy water. Nobody looks there.

dialogue.speaker: mara
dialogue.text: The frost is so hard that the window has ferns of ice. Miez watches them as if they might move.

dialogue.speaker: mara
dialogue.text: After the priest left, I read the notebook again. On a later page, there is a note with my name on it.

dialogue.speaker: mara
dialogue.text: "Mara. The bistro needs someone who cooks for people, not for money. The cabbage rolls need the same thing. The rest is in this notebook. Do not let them sell the cat."

dialogue.speaker: mama
dialogue.text: She knew your father very well.

dialogue.speaker: tata
dialogue.text: I never wanted to sell the cat.

page.text: A later page of Mamaia’s notebook: a short note in handwriting fills the page, beside a pressed sprig of basil.

events.title: The memorial of the fortieth day
events.line: Cook the memorial meal of the fortieth day, in the village.

scene.text: The village churchyard in snow. Mourners with candles stand before the church, among them Mara, Ilie, Eszter, and Sorin, beside a table with colivă and colaci.

opening.speaker: mama
opening.text: Two plates of colivă, one for the church and one for the table. Use her old dish. She would check.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Colaci and a bean dip for the neighbours who come to remember her. Half the village says that Mamaia fed them once. The other half says twice.

dialogue.speaker: mama
dialogue.text: The fortieth day falls on Tuesday, but we hold the memorial on Saturday. Saturday belongs to the dead.

dialogue.speaker: mara
dialogue.text: So we go back to the village. Colivă again, colaci again, and beans.

dialogue.speaker: tata
dialogue.text: And the notary. He reads the will after the meal. I asked him to read it before, but he has principles.

dialogue.speaker: mama
dialogue.text: Her house is full of things to sort. Mind her crate, her sack, and her linen. She labelled nothing and remembered everything.

dialogue.speaker: mara
dialogue.text: The notary read the will in the cold front room of the bistro. Mamaia left her house to Mama, her savings to the church roof, and the bistro to me.

dialogue.speaker: tata
dialogue.text: And the cat?

dialogue.speaker: mara
dialogue.text: "The cat goes where the bistro goes." It is in the will.

dialogue.speaker: mara
dialogue.text: I stood in the dark room and saw her at the stove. I am going to open the bistro again.

dialogue.speaker: mama
dialogue.text: I know. I knew at New Year.

events.title: The farewell dinner
events.line: Cook the farewell dinner before Mara leaves for the village.

scene.text: Mara waits at a bus stop of the city at dawn, with a suitcase and a cat basket, and Miez looks out through its grille.

opening.speaker: mama
opening.text: Two pots, from the notebook. This time I cook them for you, not for the notebook.

opening.speaker: tata
opening.text: Two pogăcele for the bus. The village is far, and the bus does not stop for anybody’s stomach.

opening.title: The last dinner in the city

dialogue.speaker: mama
dialogue.text: Your last dinner in the city. I am cooking the cabbage rolls from the notebook again.

dialogue.speaker: tata
dialogue.text: And I make pogăcele for the journey. Nobody leaves this flat with an empty bag.

dialogue.speaker: mara
dialogue.text: Miez knows. He sat in my suitcase all morning, and now he refuses to go in his basket.

dialogue.speaker: mara
dialogue.text: Mama, these are right. These are exactly right.

dialogue.speaker: mama
dialogue.text: I cooked them for you. That was the missing thing.

dialogue.speaker: tata
dialogue.text: Here is some money from us. It is not much, but it pays for the first days, until the bistro pays for itself.

dialogue.speaker: tata
dialogue.text: And our blessing. That one costs nothing, and it lasts longer.

dialogue.speaker: mara
dialogue.text: At dawn, I took the first bus to the village. Miez rode in his basket and complained for the whole journey.

rooms.label: mourning
rooms.text: The kitchen of the family flat in the city, in winter. A cloth covers the mirror, and a candle burns beside a photograph of Mamaia Paraschiva with a black ribbon. The window shows apartment blocks under snow, and the glass of the balcony door shows the pickle barrel.

rooms.label: Christmas
rooms.text: Fir branches hang over the kitchen door, a basket of colaci waits on the table, and the paper star of the carol singers leans by the window.

rooms.label: the new year
rooms.text: Paper streamers from the midnight table hang over the cupboard, and frost ferns cover the window.

rooms.label: the farewell
rooms.text: A packed suitcase and an empty cat basket wait by the kitchen door.
